column2: Good eye.
Take them anyway
Nothing happened. You felt great, actually.
You were dizzy all day.
The nurse thanked you.
It's Halloween at the nursing home.
Dress as a ghost
You scared three people.
Hand out candy
Kids from the neighborhood came trick-or-treating.
Eat all the candy
Worth it.
The Wi-Fi is down again and you can't video call your kids.
Fix it yourself
You unplugged it and plugged it back in. Genius.
You made it worse.
Fixed by dinner.
Write a letter instead
Old school.
{n} accused you of stealing {his} reading glasses.
Prove your innocence
They were on top of {his} head.
You had them. You honestly didn't know.
Start a feud
You now glare at each other at every meal.
Buy {him} new glasses
{n} was touched.
A big storm knocked out the power.
Best night in years.
It passed eventually.
Help the staff
You held a flashlight for two hours.
Your new neighbor, {n}, is recovering from a hip replacement.
{n} was grateful for the company.
{He} read every single one.
You were never close.
You think the art contest was rigged for {n}.
Demand a recount
You won on the recount!
Still lost.
Gracious in defeat.
You sulked for a week.
The residents are having a fancy tea party.
Wear your best hat
Best hat in the room.
Spike the tea
Nobody knew. Everyone was very happy.
The staff found out.
Tea is overrated.
Your kid promised to take you out for lunch this weekend.
Get ready early
You went to your favorite diner!
They cancelled at the last minute.
Expect nothing
They came! You were surprised.
They didn't come.
{n} had a great time.
The 1,000-piece puzzle in the lounge is missing one piece.
Search everywhere
Found it under the couch!
It's gone forever.
Make a new piece
It almost fits.
The new exercise instructor is very enthusiastic.
Keep up
You kept up!
You had to sit down.
Do half the moves
Half is fine.
You went to lunch early.
A nurse bought you a scratch-off lottery ticket.
Scratch it
You won! The whole floor celebrated.
{n} didn't win either, but appreciated it.
You'll scratch it on a lucky day.
{n} won't stop telling the same war story.
Listen again
{He} got to the part about the mule. Classic.
Tell your own story
Now you're both talking at once.
{He} kept talking anyway.
There's a surprise room inspection.
Hide your contraband snacks
They didn't find them.
Snacks confiscated.
Clean quickly
Charm the inspector
You passed with flying colors.
It's Valentine's Day at the nursing home.
{n} sent one back!
{n} gave it to someone else.
Make cards for everyone
You're very popular now.
Just another day.
You found an old photo of yourself at twenty.
Show everyone
Everyone said you were gorgeous.
Reminisce alone
Those were the days.
Frame it
It's on your nightstand now.
A teenager is teaching a class on smartphones.
Take the class
You learned what an emoji is.
Say you already know it all
You did not know it all.
Heckle the teenager
The teen was not amused.
The doctor says you're in great shape for your age.
Celebrate with cake
Earned it.
Ask for proof
The doctor showed you the chart. You didn't understand it.
{n} said {his} doctor said {he}'s in even better shape.
Come Home?
Your kid visited and asked if you want to come live with them instead.
You packed your bags. You're going home!
Their spouse said no. You're staying.
Say you like it here
You've made friends here.
Ask for time to think
They said the offer stands.
It snowed and the residents want to build a snowman.
Best snowman ever. It has dentures.
Start a snowball fight
You hit {n} square in the back.
You slipped on the ice.
Watch from inside
Hot cocoa by the window.
{n} appointed {him}self "hall monitor" and keeps writing you up.
{He} wrote you up for ignoring {him}.
Run against {him} for hall monitor
You won the election!
{He} won by a landslide.
Report {him} to the staff
The staff took away {his} clipboard.
Golden Oaks Senior Living
Willow Creek Care Center
Maple Grove Retirement Home
Autumn Leaves Manor
{k} sat you down. "{Parent}, we've been talking. We think it's time for a nursing home."
{k} showed you a brochure for {home}. "Look, they have a pool!"
{k} said, "We can't take care of you anymore. {home} has a bed open."
{k} said, "It's for your own safety. You left the stove on again."
{k} said, "You'll make friends there! And they have bingo every night!"
My friend {1} and I had a moment: {2}.
{1} I now live at {2}.
I agreed to move into a nursing home.
You packed up your things and moved into {1}.
My kids put me in a nursing home even though I refused.
{1} didn't listen. A week later, you were living at {2}.
My kids wanted to put me in a nursing home. I refused.
{1} backed off. For now.
I guilt-tripped my kids out of putting me in a nursing home.
After everything I did for you? {1} dropped the subject immediately.
My kids put me in a nursing home after I tried to guilt-trip them.
Didn't Work
{1} wasn't having it. You moved into {2} that weekend.
You no longer live in the nursing home.
Life at {1}: {2}.
Your mother {n} gave you a penny to spend at the general store. The candy jars are calling.
Buy licorice whips
I spent my penny on licorice whips.
Save it in your bank
I dropped my penny in my tin bank.
A man in goggles just rattled down Main Street in a horseless carriage. Your friend {n} wants to chase it.
Run after it
I chased a motor car down Main Street with {n}.
I chased the motor car and tripped in the road.
Shout "Get a horse!"
I shouted "Get a horse!" at the motor car like the old men do.
The family finally has a telephone, and it's on a party line. You can hear the neighbors gossiping when you pick it up.
Listen in
I listened in on the neighbors' telephone gossip.
I got caught listening in on the party line.
Hang up politely
I hung up the telephone without eavesdropping.
Newsboys are shouting that President McKinley has been shot in Buffalo. Theodore Roosevelt will be president.
Pray for the President
I prayed for President McKinley.
Read every paper
I read every newspaper about the McKinley shooting.
The papers say two bicycle makers from Ohio flew a machine through the air at Kitty Hawk.
Believe it
I read about the Wright brothers flying and dreamed of the sky.
Call it a hoax
I said the flying machine story was a hoax.
A new nickelodeon opened downtown. For a nickel you can watch moving pictures in the dark.
Spend your nickel
I spent a nickel at the nickelodeon and watched The Great Train Robbery.
Save your nickel
I saved my nickel instead of going to the nickelodeon.
The circulation man is looking for boys and girls to sell papers on the corner before school.
I sold newspapers on the corner shouting "Extra! Extra!"
I turned down selling newspapers.
The mill foreman says children your age can earn a few cents tending the spinning frames. Your family could use the money.
Go to work
I went to work in the mill for a few cents a day.
I stayed in school instead of going to the mill.
San Francisco Quake
A terrible earthquake and fire have destroyed most of San Francisco. Churches are collecting for the survivors.
Give to the relief fund
I gave to the San Francisco relief fund.
Read the stories
I read the newspaper stories about the San Francisco earthquake.
Everyone is talking about a book called The Jungle, about filthy meatpacking plants in Chicago.
I read The Jungle and couldn't look at sausage the same way.
Stop eating sausage
I gave up sausage after hearing about The Jungle.
Henry Ford's Model T is the talk of the town. The dealer lets you crank one up for a test drive.
Take it for a spin
I took a Model T out for a spin.
The Model T's crank kicked back and nearly broke my arm.
Stick with horses
I said I'd stick with horses.
Your father {n} came home with a stuffed bear everyone is calling a "Teddy" after the President.
Hug it
My father gave me a teddy bear and I never let go of it.
Throw it in the corner
I tossed the teddy bear in the corner.
World's Fair
The World's Fair is in town with electric lights, ice cream cones and a giant Ferris wheel.
Ride the Ferris wheel
I rode the giant Ferris wheel at the World's Fair.
Try an ice cream cone
I tried an ice cream cone at the World's Fair.
See the electric lights
I gazed at the electric lights at the World's Fair.
A family just off the boat from Europe moved in next door. They don't speak a word of English.
Bring them bread
I brought bread to the new immigrant family next door.
I kept my distance from the new neighbors.
The electric company is wiring your street. For a fee they'll run electric lights into your house.
Wire the house
I had electric lights put in the house.
Stick with kerosene
I kept using kerosene lamps.
Halley's Comet
Halley's Comet is blazing across the sky. Peddlers are selling "comet pills" to protect you from its poison gas.
Watch the comet
I watched Halley's Comet blaze across the night sky.
Buy comet pills
I bought comet pills from a peddler. Nothing happened.
The "unsinkable" Titanic hit an iceberg and sank. More than 1,500 people are dead.
Read the survivor lists
I read the Titanic survivor lists in the newspaper.
Swear off ocean liners
I swore I'd never set foot on an ocean liner after the Titanic.
spouse
Women are marching downtown demanding the vote. Your {rel}, {n}, wants to know whose side you're on.
March with them
I marched for women's suffrage.
I stayed home from the suffrage march.
Your friend {n} just got a new safety bicycle and offers to let you ride it.
Take a ride
I rode {n}'s new bicycle around town.
I crashed {n}'s bicycle into a hitching post.
Watch instead
I watched {n} ride the bicycle.
The circus train rolled in overnight. Elephants are parading down Main Street.
Water the elephants for a ticket
I carried water for the elephants and got a free circus ticket.
Watch the parade
I watched the circus parade down Main Street.
Congress has started a federal income tax. People are grumbling about it everywhere.
I complained about the new income tax.
Call it fair
I said the income tax was only fair.
You're getting your {rel} {n}'s old clothes again. The knees are patched and the sleeves are too long.
Complain to Mother
I complained about wearing {n}'s old clothes.
Your {rel} {n} needs one more player for stickball in the street.
I played stickball in the street with {n}.
I broke a neighbor's window playing stickball with {n}.
I stayed inside instead of playing stickball.
Birth of a Nation
A new moving picture called The Birth of a Nation is causing riots and protests in several cities.
Join the protest
I joined the protest against The Birth of a Nation.
I stayed out of the Birth of a Nation fuss.
A giant tank of molasses burst in Boston and flooded the streets, killing 21 people.
Read about it
I read about the Boston molasses flood.
Laugh in disbelief
I laughed at the molasses flood story until I learned people died.
The Nineteenth Amendment passed. Women can vote! Your {rel}, {n}, is heading to the polls for the first time.
I went to the polls with {n} on the first election women could vote.
I stayed home on election day.
Your friend {n} knows a password to a speakeasy hidden behind a barbershop.
Go in
I drank bathtub gin at a speakeasy with {n}.
The speakeasy got raided while {n} and I were inside.
Stay dry
I stayed away from the speakeasy.
A bootlegger named {n} offers you good money to drive a truck of whiskey across the county line.
Drive the load
I ran a truckload of bootleg whiskey for {n}.
Prohibition agents stopped my whiskey truck and seized everything.
I refused to run whiskey for {n}.
With Prohibition on, folks are brewing their own gin in bathtubs.
Brew some yourself
I brewed bathtub gin in the cellar.
My bathtub gin was poison and I got terribly sick.
Not worth it
I didn't brew any bathtub gin.
Your friend {n} bobbed {his} hair and wants you to come do the Charleston at the dance hall.
I danced the Charleston all night with {n}.
Say it's scandalous
I told {n} the Charleston was scandalous.
Your father {n} brought home a radio set. The whole family is crowded around it listening to music from far away.
Listen all evening
We listened to the radio all evening.
Fiddle with the dial
I fiddled with the radio dial to pick up distant stations.
A shoeshine boy gives you a hot stock tip. "Buy on margin, everybody's getting rich!"
Buy on margin
I bought stock on margin on a shoeshine boy's tip.
The shoeshine boy's stock tip went bust.
Keep your money in the bank
I ignored the hot stock tip.
Charles Lindbergh flew alone across the Atlantic to Paris! There's a ticker-tape parade in New York.
Cheer for Lucky Lindy
I cheered for Lindbergh's flight across the Atlantic.
Dream of flying
I dreamed of flying like Lindbergh.
The Jazz Singer is playing, a moving picture where the actors actually talk!
I saw The Jazz Singer, the first talking picture.
Wait for it to come back
I skipped the talking picture.
Babe Ruth and the Yankees are in town. Tickets are cheap in the bleachers.
Go to the game
I watched Babe Ruth hit one out of the park.
Listen on the radio
I listened to the Yankees game on the radio.
Your friend {n} entered a dance marathon with a cash prize. Couples dance for days until they drop.
Join as {his} partner
I danced for three days straight with {n} and won the prize.
I collapsed on the second day of the dance marathon.
I watched the dance marathon.
Buy on Credit
The department store says you can buy a new washing machine "on the installment plan" for a few dollars a month.
Buy it on credit
I bought a washing machine on the installment plan.
Pay cash or go without
I refused to buy anything on credit.
A Tennessee schoolteacher named Scopes is on trial for teaching evolution.
Side with Scopes
I sided with Scopes in the Monkey Trial.
Side with the Bible
I sided with the prosecution in the Monkey Trial.
A cartoon mouse named Mickey is whistling on a steamboat at the picture show.
Laugh until it hurts
I laughed at Mickey Mouse in Steamboat Willie.
Draw your own cartoon
I drew my own cartoon after seeing Mickey Mouse.
The stock market has crashed! Men are weeping on Wall Street and the banks are swamped.
Rush to the bank
I rushed to the bank after the stock market crash.
I tried to stay calm after the stock market crash.
Father's Stocks
Your father {n} sat at the kitchen table all night staring at the newspaper. His stocks are worthless.
Sit with him
I sat with my father after he lost everything in the crash.
Hide in your room
I hid in my room while my father stared at the newspaper.
A crowd is pounding on the bank doors. People say the bank is about to fail and take everyone's savings with it.
I got some of my savings out before the bank closed its doors.
The bank shut its doors before I reached the window. My savings were gone.
I left my money in the bank.
I trusted the bank, and it failed with all my savings.
The breadline outside the mission stretches around the block. A bowl of soup and a heel of bread are free.
Get in line
I stood in the breadline for soup and bread.
Too proud
I was too proud to stand in the breadline.
Al Capone himself opened a soup kitchen in Chicago. Your church needs volunteers for its own.
Ladle soup
I volunteered at the soup kitchen.
Can't spare the time
I didn't volunteer at the soup kitchen.
Brother, Can You Spare a Dime?
A man in a worn suit who used to be a banker asks you for a dime.
Give him a dime
I gave a dime to a down-and-out former banker.
Walk past
I walked past a man begging for a dime.
A shantytown of tin and cardboard shacks has sprung up by the river. People call it a Hooverville.
Bring them food
I brought food to the families in the Hooverville.
Stay away
I stayed away from the Hooverville.
Riding the Rails
Your friend {n} plans to hop a freight train and look for work out west.
I rode the rails west with {n} looking for work.
A railroad bull beat me and threw me off the freight train.
I stayed home while {n} rode the rails.
The foreman says the plant is cutting back. Half the men are getting pink slips this week.
Beg to keep your job
I begged the foreman to keep my job.
I accepted that I might be laid off.
Supper tonight is a "Hoover stew" of whatever was left in the cupboard, and dandelion greens from the yard.
Clean your plate
I ate every bite of the Hoover stew.
I complained about the Depression supper.
Flour Sack Dress
Your mother {n} sewed you new clothes out of printed flour sacks.
Wear them happily
I wore my new flour sack clothes.
Feel embarrassed
I was embarrassed by my flour sack clothes.
The landlord nailed an eviction notice to the door. The family is three months behind on rent.
Plead with the landlord
I pleaded with the landlord for more time.
The landlord put our furniture out on the sidewalk.
Gather the neighbors
The neighbors helped carry our furniture back inside after the eviction.
Taking in Boarders
Your mother {n} says the family will have to take in boarders to pay the mortgage.
Give up your room
I gave up my room for a boarder.
Grumble about it
I grumbled about strangers living in the house.
Moving Back Home
Your {rel} {n} lost {his} job and needs a place to stay.
I took my {rel} {n} in during the Depression.
I couldn't take in my {rel} {n}.
Men are selling apples on street corners for a nickel apiece. You could sell some too.
Sell apples
I sold apples on the street corner for a nickel apiece.
Shine shoes instead
I shined shoes on the corner for pennies.
Empire State Building
The Empire State Building is finished, the tallest building in the world.
Visit the top
I rode to the top of the Empire State Building.
Look at the photos
I looked at newspaper photos of the Empire State Building.
Charles Lindbergh's baby son has been kidnapped from his crib. The whole country is searching.
Pray for the baby
I prayed for the Lindbergh baby.
Lock your windows
I started locking the windows after the Lindbergh kidnapping.
Thousands of out-of-work veterans marched on Washington for their war bonuses. The Army drove them out with tear gas.
Side with the veterans
I sided with the Bonus Army veterans.
Stay out of politics
I stayed out of the Bonus Army argument.
President Roosevelt is on the radio, calmly explaining the bank holiday. "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself."
I listened to President Roosevelt's fireside chat.
I turned off the fireside chat.
The Civilian Conservation Corps is hiring young men to plant trees and build parks for $30 a month, $25 of it sent home.
I joined the CCC and planted trees in the national forest.
I didn't join the CCC.
The Works Progress Administration is hiring men to build roads, bridges and schools.
I took a WPA job building a new bridge.
Keep looking
I kept looking for private work.
Beer Is Back
Prohibition is over! Taverns are opening their doors and the beer is flowing legally again.
Raise a glass
I raised a glass the day Prohibition ended.
Stay sober
I stayed sober the day Prohibition ended.
A wall of black dust is rolling across the plains, blotting out the sun. The Dust Bowl has come to your door.
Stuff wet rags in the windows
I stuffed wet rags in the windows during the dust storm.
Run for the cellar
I hid in the cellar while the black blizzard raged.
I caught dust pneumonia after the storm.
Your father {n} says the farm is finished. He wants to pack the family into the old truck and head for California.
Go with him
Our family packed up the truck and headed west to California.
Stay and fight for the farm
I stayed behind to fight for the family farm.
Your shoes have holes in the soles. Your mother {n} cut cardboard to put inside them.
I stuffed cardboard in my shoes and made do.
I cried about the holes in my shoes.
The Lone Ranger is on the radio tonight. Hi-yo, Silver!
Listen with the family
I listened to The Lone Ranger on the radio.
Read a dime novel instead
I read a dime novel instead of listening to the radio.
Congress passed the Social Security Act. Workers will get a pension when they grow old.
Sounds wonderful
I was glad to hear about Social Security.
Call it socialism
I called Social Security socialism.
Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the Berlin Olympics, right under Hitler's nose.
I cheered for Jesse Owens at the Berlin Olympics.
Start running
I started running after hearing about Jesse Owens.
The airship Hindenburg burst into flames while landing in New Jersey. "Oh, the humanity!"
Listen to the radio report
I listened to the radio report of the Hindenburg disaster.
Swear off airships
I swore I'd never ride in an airship after the Hindenburg.
Amelia Earhart Lost
Amelia Earhart has vanished over the Pacific during her flight around the world.
Hope she's found
I hoped Amelia Earhart would be found.
Wonder what happened
I wondered what happened to Amelia Earhart.
War of the Worlds
The radio says Martians have landed in New Jersey! People are running into the streets.
I panicked during the War of the Worlds broadcast. It was only a radio play.
Recognize Orson Welles
I recognized the War of the Worlds broadcast was just a radio play.
The Wizard of Oz
The Wizard of Oz is playing in glorious color. Everyone is humming "Over the Rainbow."
I saw The Wizard of Oz in Technicolor.
See Gone with the Wind instead
I saw Gone with the Wind instead.
World of Tomorrow
The New York World's Fair is showing off the "World of Tomorrow," including a strange box called television.
See the television
I saw television for the first time at the World's Fair.
Ride the parachute jump
I rode the parachute jump at the World's Fair.
Your {rel} {n} says you can't afford meat this week. Supper will be beans again.
Agree to tighten your belt
My {rel} and I tightened our belts and ate beans all week.
Argue about money
My {rel} {n} and I argued about money.
No Christmas Presents
There's no money for Christmas presents this year. Your {rel} {n} is staring at the empty spot under the tree.
Carve {him} a wooden toy
I carved a wooden toy for my {rel} {n} for Christmas.
Explain about hard times
I told my {rel} {n} there would be no presents this year.
Pawn the Ring
The rent is due and the only thing of value left is the family wedding ring.
I pawned the family wedding ring to pay the rent.
Keep it no matter what
I refused to pawn the wedding ring.
A hobo named {n} knocks at the back door asking for food. There's a chalk mark on your fence saying "kind lady lives here."
I gave a hungry hobo a plate of food at the back door.
Trade food for chores
{n} split our firewood in exchange for a meal.
I sent a hungry hobo away from the door.
A new board game called Monopoly lets you pretend to be a rich landlord, a fine fantasy these days.
I played Monopoly all night and bought Boardwalk.
Play marbles instead
I played marbles instead of Monopoly.
The bank is auctioning off a neighbor's farm. Farmers are gathering to bid pennies and give it back to him.
Bid a penny
I bid a penny at the penny auction and helped give the farm back.
I stayed away from the penny auction.
Money is so tight that you and your {rel} {n} are sharing a bed with two other cousins.
Make the best of it
I shared a bed with {n} and the cousins.
Fight for blanket space
I fought {n} for the blanket every night.
Your father {n} says he's going to look for work in another state. He doesn't know when he'll be back.
Beg him to stay
I begged my father not to leave.
Promise to help Mother
I promised my father I'd help Mother while he was gone.
Scrap Paper Drive
The scouts are collecting old newspapers and tin cans for the war effort.
Collect a wagonload
I collected a wagonload of scrap for the war effort.
I skipped the scrap drive.
Rosie the Riveter
Your friend {n} took a job riveting bomber wings at the aircraft plant. They need more workers.
I took a job at the aircraft plant with {n}.
Stay at home
I didn't take a war plant job.
Butter is rationed. The margarine comes white, with a packet of yellow dye you knead in yourself.
Knead in the color
I kneaded the yellow dye into the margarine.
Eat it white
I ate the margarine white.
Nylon is going into parachutes. Women are drawing seams up the backs of their legs to fake stockings.
Draw on seams
I drew stocking seams on my legs with eyebrow pencil.
Go without
I went without stockings.
Your mother {n} is writing V-mail letters to the boys overseas. She wants you to add a few lines.
Write something cheerful
I wrote a cheerful V-mail to the soldiers overseas.
Too busy
I didn't write any V-mail.
Before the cartoon at the picture show, there's a newsreel of the fighting overseas.
Watch closely
I watched the war newsreels at the picture show.
Cover your eyes
I covered my eyes during the newsreel.
The Atomic Bomb
A single bomb destroyed the Japanese city of Hiroshima. The papers call it an "atomic bomb."
Feel relieved the war will end
I was relieved the atomic bomb would end the war.
Feel horrified
I was horrified by the atomic bomb.
President Roosevelt has died at Warm Springs. Harry Truman is president. People are weeping in the streets.
I mourned President Roosevelt.
Wonder about Truman
I wondered what kind of president Truman would be.
Your {rel} {n} says all your friends are having babies now that the war is over.
Talk about a family
My {rel} {n} and I talked about having children.
I told {n} I wasn't ready for children.
A new suburb of identical little houses is going up outside the city. Veterans can buy one with nothing down.
Tour a model home
I toured a model home in the new suburb.
Stay in the city
I stayed in the city.
Your father {n} brought home a television set. The whole block is crowding into the living room.
Watch Howdy Doody
I watched Howdy Doody on our new television.
Adjust the rabbit ears
I fiddled with the television's rabbit ears all evening.
Jackie Robinson took the field for the Brooklyn Dodgers, breaking baseball's color line.
Cheer for him
I cheered for Jackie Robinson.
Go to a game
I went to see Jackie Robinson play.
Duck and Cover
The teacher is drilling the class to duck under your desks in case of an atomic attack.
Take it seriously
I practiced ducking and covering under my desk.
Giggle with your friends
I giggled through the duck and cover drill.
A salesman is selling backyard fallout shelters, stocked with canned food and water.
Build one
I built a fallout shelter in the backyard.
Take your chances
I didn't build a fallout shelter.
There's a polio scare this summer. Your mother {n} says no swimming pools and no crowds.
Obey her
I stayed away from swimming pools during the polio scare.
Sneak to the pool
I snuck off to the swimming pool.
I caught polio and spent weeks in an iron lung ward.
Dr. Salk's polio vaccine works! Children are lining up at school for their shots.
Get the shot
I got the Salk polio vaccine.
Avoid the needle
I avoided getting the polio shot.
Rock and Roll
Your friend {n} has a new record by a singer named Elvis Presley. Your parents think it's the devil's music.
Dance to it
I danced to Elvis records with {n}.
Agree with your parents
I told {n} rock and roll was the devil's music.
Your friend {n} wants to go to the drive-in to see a monster picture.
I went to the drive-in with {n}.
I skipped the drive-in.
There's a sock hop in the school gymnasium Friday night.
Ask someone to dance
I asked someone to dance at the sock hop.
I got turned down at the sock hop.
Stand by the punch bowl
I stood by the punch bowl at the sock hop.
Every kid on the block has a hula hoop.
Hoop for an hour
I hula hooped for an hour straight.
Can't get the hang of it
I couldn't keep the hula hoop up.
The Russians launched a satellite called Sputnik. You can hear it beeping on the radio.
Look for it in the sky
I watched for Sputnik crossing the night sky.
Worry about the Russians
I worried the Russians were winning the space race.
The new diner has jukeboxes at every booth and milkshakes for a quarter.
Order a milkshake
I had a milkshake at the diner.
Play the jukebox
I fed nickels to the diner jukebox.
Walt Disney opened a giant amusement park in California called Disneyland.
Beg your parents to go
I begged my parents to take me to Disneyland.
Watch it on TV
I watched the Disneyland opening on television.
Your {rel} {n} brought home TV dinners, a whole meal in an aluminum tray.
Eat in front of the TV
My {rel} and I ate TV dinners in front of the television.
Insist on a real supper
I insisted on a home-cooked supper.
Kennedy Nixon Debate
Kennedy and Nixon are debating on television. Nixon looks sweaty and pale.
Root for Kennedy
I rooted for Kennedy in the televised debate.
Root for Nixon
I rooted for Nixon in the televised debate.
Cuban Missile Crisis
The Russians have missiles in Cuba. Everyone fears nuclear war could start any day.
Stock the cellar
I stocked the cellar with canned food during the Cuban Missile Crisis.
Pray for peace
I prayed for peace during the Cuban Missile Crisis.
